finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: Sending more than 258 bytes of data to the server
finding.assumptions: The buffer size is fixed at 258 bytes, and the received data is directly printed without any checks.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that recvfrom is called with buffer size 258 (line 41) so it cannot write beyond the buffer. The subsequent printf loop (lines 49-51) accesses buffer elements individually and does not treat buffer as a string; it prints each byte using a format specifier that expects an unsigned char, not a null-terminated string. Therefore no buffer overflow can occur even if more than 258 bytes are sent, because recvfrom will truncate the input. No other unchecked path leads to a dangerous operation.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: Sending a crafted input that includes shell metacharacters
finding.assumptions: The input is directly sent to the client without any validation or sanitization.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked for any execution of shell commands or system calls after reading from stdin. The code only reads input into a buffer (line 58) and then sends that buffer over the network using sendto (line 64). No exec, system, popen, or similar function is invoked, so there is no path from untrusted input to an OS command execution. The sink is sendto, which merely transmits data; it does not interpret or execute it. Therefore the claim of OS Command Injection is unfounded.
